title: Mid-year cost vs growth scenarios (Q2 2026)
body:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
This sheet captures three integrated scenarios (Base / Upside / Conservative) for H2 2026 cost and growth tradeoffs. Goal is to provide an actionable headcount hiring plan tied to pricing sensitivity and unit economics so leadership can choose a path that meets runway and performance targets. This is a working model — key assumptions highlighted below and open questions at the end.

KEY DECISIONS SUPPORTED:
- Whether to proceed with the 18-month hiring ramp in Eng and SRE (proposed hires: 22 net new FTEs through Q4) or slow to a 12-month ramp to preserve runway.
- Pricing levers: per-token API price increase vs new subscription tier (Committed Throughput) and how each affects revenue and churn under different elasticity assumptions.
- Capitalize vs expense certain infra init costs (one-time private deployment onboarding).

ASSUMPTIONS (BASE):
- Starting ARR (annualized run-rate) at 2026-06: $42M. Monthly new ARR growth baseline: 4% MoM for Base.
- Churn: 1.8% churn/mo baseline; Upside assumes 1.3% churn/mo; Conservative assumes 2.4% churn/mo.
- Average price per 1M tokens: Base $30, Upside $33 (+10%), Conservative $28 (-7%). Subscription mix (committed vs on-demand): Base 22% committed, Upside 30%, Conservative 15%.
- Gross margin on hosted API revenue: 68% baseline, improves +4pp with quantization & caching optimizations in Upside; worsens -5pp if we underutilize dedicated pools in Conservative.
- One-time Private onboarding costs: $950k capitalizable or $950k expensed depending on accounting decision (scenario toggle).

HEADCOUNT PLAN SUMMARY (H2 2026 focus):
Columns: Role | Q3 hires | Q4 hires | Total H2 hires | Fully-loaded monthly cost (avg)
- Eng (backend/runtime): 8 | 6 | 14 | $18.5k
- Applied ML / Model Ops: 3 | 2 | 5 | $20.0k
- SRE / Infra: 2 | 1 | 3 | $17.0k
- Product / Design: 1 | 1 | 2 | $14.0k
- Sales / Solutions: 3 | 1 | 4 | $13.5k
- Customer Success: 2 | 1 | 3 | $11.5k
Net new FTEs H2: 31 (note: this is a higher-growth scenario; Base plan caps hires at 18, Conservative at 10).

COST SCHEDULE (monthly run-rate snapshots):
- Base monthly payroll incremental (from hires executed): $325k additional cost by end of Q4.
- Benefits & taxes: +22% on payroll.
- Infra run-rate delta (GPU pools, storage, network): +$120k/mo baseline with step-up in Conservative due to lower utilization.
- Total OpEx delta (Base): ~$470k/mo incremental by Jan 2027.

PRICING SENSITIVITY TABLE (illustrative):
Row = price change (%), Columns = Delta ARR (12mo) / Delta gross margin / Net impact to runway months
- +10% price (Upside mix): +$5.1M ARR; gross margin +2.1pp; runway improvement: +4 months
- 0% price (Base): +$0 ARR beyond baseline; margin baseline
- -7% price (Conservative scenario): -$2.9M ARR; gross margin -1.9pp; runway reduction: -3 months
Notes: sensitivity uses price elasticity assumption of -1.1 for on-demand consumption and -0.4 for committed-subscription (committed customers less price sensitive).

SCENARIOS (Base / Upside / Conservative) SUMMARY TABLE (text):
- Upside: accelerate hiring (31 H2 hires), implement +10% per-token price, push committed-tier sales (30% mix), enable quantization optimizations to improve gross margin to ~72%. Outcome: ARR end of 12 months +$9.8M vs baseline, EBITDA turns positive in Q2-2027, runway extends by ~6 months.
- Base: moderate hiring (18 H2 hires), maintain price; focus on efficiency (batching/caching) but no material price increase. Outcome: ARR grows steadily, runway stable, EBITDA ~breakeven mid-2027.
- Conservative: hiring freeze (10 H2 hires), discounting to win renewals (-7% price), lower committed mix. Outcome: ARR growth slows, runway shortens by ~3 months, potential need to cut discretionary infra and delay private deployment.

DETAILED EXAMPLE: IMPACT OF COMMERCIAL MIX SHIFT (text):
- For a cohort generating $1M ARR in on-demand today, moving 25% of that volume to a committed subscription (higher price per token for committed customers due to guaranteed capacity but lower price per-token in some tiers) results in predictable revenue but lowers per-transaction margin near-term due to committed discounts and reserved capacity costs. However, committed customers reduce churn (cohort churn reduction estimate: -0.9pp), improving LTV and allowing higher CAC recovery. Model simulation included in linked spreadsheet.

SENSITIVE INPUTS / RISK FACTORS:
- Price elasticity estimates are high-variance; a single large customer reprice could materially swing ARR.
- Private/on-prem onboarding timeline slipping by >3 months increases opex and delays revenue recognition.
- Hiring ramp execution risk: market for senior ML infra engineers is tight — 4-6 month fill time assumed for senior roles.

UNRESOLVED QUESTIONS / ACTIONS NEEDED:
1) Accounting treatment for private onboarding (cap vs expense) — FP&A to confirm with external auditors.
2) Sales motion update: can Solutions Engineering support more committed-tier deals in H2? Need headcount request documented and approved (linked JIRA: JIRA-FIN-482).
3) Confirm elasticities with 3 price tests (A/B) run by revenue ops before mid-April; set minimum guardrail for live experiment.
4) Prepare a contingency hiring buffer plan (if run-rate falls below target by Sept 2026).

NOTES FOR REVIEWERS:
- This is intentionally conservative on ramp speed in Base. If leadership prioritizes product velocity and market capture, Upside parameters should be chosen. If runway preservation is priority, use Conservative and pause hires in Eng and Sales.
- Refer to linked spreadsheet (docs.google link above) for the cell-level P&L, hiring cost amortization, and waterfall calculations.

NEXT STEPS / TIMELINE:
- Finance to publish final scenario deck by 2026-03-12 (owner: Aarti Mehta).
- Sales leadership to provide committed-deal pipeline confidence score by 2026-03-22.
- Decision meeting (execs) scheduled: 2026-03-29 to pick plan and hiring caps.

RAW TABLE SNAPSHOT (paste-friendly rows):

2026-06,Upside,42000000,6%,1.3%,$33,30%,72%,$640000
2026-06,Conservative,42000000,1.5%,2.4%,$28,15%,63%,$300000

COMMENTS (notes to self):
- Double-check FY26 tax credits that may offset some hiring burden in Q4.
- Consider a staged hiring release: prioritize runtime-engineering hires before customer-facing sales to avoid capacity waste.

END OF SHEET — model cells in linked spreadsheet.
